claims.claim_vi: VISA, Mastercard and American Express are card networks that clear and settle funds. The acquiring bank and the issuing bank can be, and often are, different; without an intermediary each bank would have to settle with all the other banks, which is inefficient.
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: Two flows: the authorization flow happens when the customer swipes the card; the capture and settlement flow happens when the merchant wants the money at the end of the day.
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: Authorization flow: step 0 the issuing bank issues cards; step 1 the cardholder swipes the card at the POS terminal; step 2 the POS terminal sends the transaction to the acquiring bank that provided the terminal; steps 3 and 4 the acquiring bank sends it to the card network (card scheme), which sends it to the issuing bank for approval.
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: Steps 4.1 to 4.3: the issuing bank freezes the money if the transaction is approved; the approval or rejection goes back to the acquirer and the POS terminal.
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: Capture and settlement: the merchant hits capture on the POS terminal at the end of the day; the transactions go to the acquirer in batches; the acquirer sends the batch file to the card network.
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: The card network clears the transactions collected from different acquirers and sends clearing files to the issuing banks; the issuing banks confirm the files and transfer money to the acquiring banks; the acquiring bank transfers money to the merchant's bank.
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: Clearing is a process in which mutual offset transactions are netted, so the number of total transactions is reduced; the card network takes on the burden of talking to each bank and receives service fees in return.
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: The source lists "Step 4" twice in the capture flow (issuing banks confirm, and the card network clears); the lesson follows the order the text reads in and notes the repeat as a limit.
claims.verified_by: Author's general knowledge; not checked against payment-industry documentation.

design_notes_vi: Hai lược đồ ba bên cho luồng xin phép (mỗi lược đồ bắt đầu bằng bên cuối của lược đồ trước), một khung bốn bước cho phần cuối ngày, rồi một khung giải thích vì sao có mạng thẻ.
source_deviations: The source writes VISA in capitals; the lesson writes "Visa" to avoid an abbreviation that is only a brand name.
The source lists "Step 4" twice and has the clearing explanation as the last bullet; the lesson folds that explanation into the card for clearing and into the closing note.
The source says the POS terminal also receives the approval or rejection; the lesson draws the message to the acquiring bank and keeps the POS terminal in the text.
Step 0 (the issuing bank issues cards) is kept in the text and not drawn as a message.
